questions.question: What was the role of the prime minister in the planning commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ex-Officio chairman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Prime Minister of India served as the **Ex-Officio Chairman** of the Planning Commission during its existence (1950–2014).
 
• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India that formulated India’s Five-Year Plans and various economic policies.
 
• The role of the Ex-Officio Chairman was to provide strategic direction and oversee the formulation and execution of national plans.
 
• The Prime Minister, as the Ex-Officio Chairman, held ultimate authority in decision-making within the Planning Commission.
 
• In 2015, the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog, and the Prime Minister became the Ex-Officio Chairman of the NITI Aayog as well.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planning Commission**

 
 
• Established in 1950 by a resolution of the Government of India under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• The body was tasked with assessing resources and drafting Five-Year Plans to achieve economic and social goals.
 
• It functioned as an advisory body to the Government of India.
 
• It was dissolved in 2014 and replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India).
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**
 
 
• Formed on January 1, 2015, as the successor to the Planning Commission.
 
• Aims to foster cooperative federalism by involving states in the policy-making process.
 
• Focuses on long-term policy planning and innovation to achieve sustainable development goals.
 
• The Prime Minister serves as the Ex-Officio Chairman of NITI Aayog, with a Governing Council comprising Chief Ministers of states and Union Territories.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans**
 
 
• These were centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• India implemented 12 Five-Year Plans between 1951 and 2017.
 
• The first Five-Year Plan focused on agriculture, while later plans emphasized industrialization, infrastructure, and economic liberalization.
 
• After the dissolution of the Planning Commission, Five-Year Plans were replaced by long-term strategies under NITI Aayog.
 
 
 
• **Ex-Officio Position**
 
 
• The term "Ex-Officio" refers to a position held by someone by virtue of another office or role they hold.
 
• For example, the Prime Minister automatically became the Ex-Officio Chairman of the Planning Commission and now of NITI Aayog.
 
• This ensures that the highest executive authority is directly involved in strategic planning and decision-making.

questions.question: Article 40 of the Indian constitution, "Organisation of village panchayats", is a _______.

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy:-**

 
 
• Articles 36-51 of Part-IV of the Indian Constitution deals with Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). 
 
• They are borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland. 
 
• DPSPs are non-justiciable i.e non-enforceable in the court of law.
 
• They act as directives to the government to create any law.
 
• They act as the ‘instrument of instructions’.

• ​These are a set of moral obligations that are mentioned in the Constitution of India.
 
• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976.
 
• These duties are not enforceable by law but are expected to be followed by every citizen as a means of promoting a spirit of patriotism and upholding the ideals of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• Fundamental Rights:-
 
 
• FRs are known as the base of the Indian constitution & mentioned in Part III of the constitution.
 
• They prohibit unreasonable interference of the state & prevent its executive & legislature to become authoritarian, hence putting due limitations on state power.
 
 
 
• Legal right:-

• It is a claim that a person has against another person or against the state. Legal rights can be enforced through the courts.

questions.question: Originally, the Constitution of India had ________ Schedules.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Constitution of India:

 
 
• The Constitution of India is the supreme law of the land, laying down the framework that defines the political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
 
 
• Schedules in the Constitution:
 
 
• The Constitution originally had 8 schedules, but now it has 12 schedules. These schedules are lists in the Constitution that categorize and tabulate bureaucratic activity and government policy.
 
 
 
• Details of the 12 Schedules:
 
 
• First Schedule: Lists the states and territories of India.
 
• Second Schedule: Provisions related to the President, Governors, Judges, and Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
 
• Third Schedule: Forms of Oaths or Affirmations.
 
• Fourth Schedule: Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Fifth Schedule: Provisions related to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
 
• Sixth Schedule: Provisions for the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.
 
• Seventh Schedule: Division of powers between the Union and States (Union List, State List, and Concurrent List).
 
• Eighth Schedule: Lists the official languages recognized by the Constitution.
 
• Ninth Schedule: Contains acts and laws that are exempt from judicial review.
 
• Tenth Schedule: Provisions related to disqualification of members on the ground of defection.
 
• Eleventh Schedule: Specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats.
 
• Twelfth Schedule: Specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities.

questions.question: An alliance formed by political parties after elections when no party has been able to get adequate seats to form a clear majority is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**coalition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A coalition government is a type of government where two or more political parties join together in parliament/ assembly to run the government and agree on a policy program.

 
 
• A coalition government is a cabinet of a parliamentary government in which several parties cooperate.
 
• The usual reason given for this arrangement is that no party on its own can achieve a majority in the parliament.
 
• A coalition government might also be created in a time of national difficulty or crisis, for example during wartime, to give a government the high degree of perceived political legitimacy it desires and also playing a role in diminishing internal political strife.
 
• In such times, parties have formed all-party coalitions (national unity governments, grand coalitions).
 
• If a coalition collapses a confidence vote is held or a motion of no confidence is taken.
 
• A coalition government is oftentimes considered a very weak form of government because there is no majority party.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is introduced by Finance Minister.
 
• It is introduced in Lok Sabha.
 
• It gives the legal power to the Govt. for expenditure.

• A coalition government is formed when multiple political parties join hands to create a majority in the legislature.
 
• This type of government usually arises when no single party gains a sufficient number of seats to form a majority on its own.
 
• Coalition governments are based on a consensus programme agenda agreed upon by all the participating parties.
 
• Such a government requires constant negotiation and compromise among the member parties to maintain stability.

• It usually results in a more stable and efficient administration as compared to coalition governments.
 
 
 
• **Presidential Government**
 
 
• This system features a president who serves as both the head of state and the head of government.
 
• It is characterized by a clear separation of powers between the executive and the legislature.
 
• Examples include the United States and Brazil.
 
 
 
• **One-Party System**
 
 
• In a one-party system, a single political party controls the government and other parties are either banned or allowed limited participation.
 
• It often leads to a lack of political pluralism and can be associated with authoritarian regimes.
 
• Examples include China and North Korea.
 
 
 
• **Consensus Programme Agenda**
 
 
• This refers to an agreed-upon set of policies and priorities that coalition parties commit to implementing together.
 
• It ensures that all coalition members have a stake in the government’s agenda, promoting cooperation and reducing conflicts.

• The National Emblem of India may only be used in accordance with the provisions of the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act-2005, and any unauthorized use is illegal.

questions.question: The ______ Amendment of the Constitution of India envisages the Gram Sabha as the foundation of the Panchayat Raj System to perform functions and powers entrusted to it by the State Legislatures.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**73rd.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **73rd Amendment of the Constitution** of India envisages the Gram Sabha as the foundation of the Panchayat Raj System to perform functions and powers entrusted to it by the State Legislatures.
 
• The Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, 1992 has added a new **part IX **consisting of 16 Articles and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution.
 
• The 73rd Amendment envisages the Gram Sabha as the foundation of the Panchayat Raj System to perform functions and powers entrusted to it by the State Legislatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The amendment provides for a three-tier Panchayat Raj System at the village, intermediate, and district levels. 
 
• Articles 243A provides that the Gram Sabha may exercise such power and perform such functions at the village level as the Legislature of a State may by law provide.
 
• The eleventh schedule of the constitution created by the 73rd Amendment contains 29 subjects on which the Panchayats shall have administrative control, Articles 243H empowers State Legislature to make provisions for imposing taxes, etc. by the panchayat.
 
• 
 
Thus, we can conclude that the **73rd Amendment of the Constitution of India, is related to Panchayats.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the political parties in India?

options.text: A political party symbol is assigned by the President of India.
India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.
All parties are registered with the Supreme Court of India.
Status of party is accorded by the Parliament.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India follows a multi-party system where multiple political parties can exist and participate in elections.
 
• Political parties in India are classified into national, state or regional level based on their performance and influence.
 
• National parties are those that have influence over a larger part of India, while state or regional parties have influence limited to specific states or regions.
 
• This classification helps in managing the democratic process and ensuring representation at both the national and state levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI)**

 
 
• The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• It administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.
 
• The ECI ensures free and fair elections in India.
 
 
 
• **Registration of Political Parties**
 
 
• Political parties in India are registered with the Election Commission of India under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
 
• Registration with the ECI is a precondition for a political party to be recognized as a national or state party.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Political Parties**
 
 
• The status of a political party, whether national or state, is determined based on its performance in elections.
 
• Criteria for recognition include the number of seats won in elections and the percentage of votes obtained.
 
 
 
• **Symbols of Political Parties**
 
 
• The Election Commission of India assigns symbols to political parties to help voters identify them during elections.
 
• Symbols play a significant role in the election process, especially for illiterate voters who may not recognize party names.
